messages:
maya (docs): Heads-up — spotted a copy/paste issue in the new mini-garden quickstart. The auth snippet in step 2 uses the old SDK import and the fenced code block is missing a backtick so it breaks when users paste. I opened a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789

sam (devex): Thanks Maya. Can you paste the failing snippet here so I can reproduce locally? I can run a quick smoke if you want.

maya (docs): Sure — snippet from the tutorial page:
```python
from redwood_inference import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
# ...
```
The docs site lost the closing ``` in the rendered page which mangled the next paragraph.

jordan (eng): I can add a small compatibility shim so both imports work for SDK5 -> SDK6 users, but docs should prefer the new `from redwood import Client` form. Also flagging the token rotation note — we reference the old env var name in one spot.

sam (devex): I pulled PR #789, ran the quickstart and hit `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named redwood_inference` — guess that's the old package name.

maya (docs): PR #789 now updates the fenced block, switches to `from redwood import Client` and adds a short migration note for SDK5 users. I also added an explicit step to export `REDWOOD_API_KEY` before running the first deploy. Need reviews and someone to flip the CI smoke job to validate copy-paste. @sam @jordan can you take a look?

lee (product): Can we also update the console screenshot in step 4? The UI moved the “Create key” button and I think users will be confused. I'll file a follow-up issue and attach a new screenshot.

deploy-bot: CI: docs/quickstart-mini-garden smoke test failed on PR #789 — traceback shows auth env var missing and the example server crashed during startup.

sam (devex): Add a note in the quickstart: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` before `python run.py`. Pushed a tiny patch to the PR to include that step and a one-line smoke script that verifies the example starts.

maya (docs): Thanks — pushed one more commit that fixes the fence, adds the env var note, and includes the smoke script under `docs/smoke/mini-garden.sh`. If you can run it locally and confirm, I’ll request final review.

sam (devex): :eyes: running now locally...

sam (devex): OK the script runs through. One thing: the example currently shows the sync client only. For serverless runtimes we should include a small async snippet too. Suggest adding a 2-line async example (aiohttp/asyncio) and a note about connection reuse.

jordan (eng): Agreed — I’ll add an async snippet and a sentence about reusing the client for connection pooling. I’ll also add a micro-compat shim so older `redwood_inference` import resolves to the new package while we finish migration docs.

maya (docs): Perfect — if we get two approvals I’ll merge and tag as `quickstart-refresh-mini-garden`. Also will open an issue to track the screenshot change and the SDK migration cross-links.

lee (product): +1, schedule merge before the next release window (tomorrow).

sam (devex): Approved and added a smoke CI test that curls the quickstart endpoint and expects HTTP 200.

deploy-bot: CI: docs/quickstart-mini-garden smoke test passed on branch maya/fix-fence after approvals.

maya (docs): Merged. Thanks all! Follow-up: filing the screenshot/migration issues and a short post in #announcements so new users know the quickstart was refreshed.
